design_goal: Let an admin connect Netskope, tune its influence on risk score, and optionally share Dune's own risk signals outward, with full visibility into what each control does, without the two-vendor category list feeling cluttered or the write-back flow feeling opaque.
constraints: RBAC scope is Full Access admin only, confirmed with stakeholder, matching the CrowdStrike precedent
Netskope base tier covers 5 of 7 categories; UI must render correctly for 1 to 7 available categories and should expect a fuller panel than CrowdStrike's by default
Connect credential model is a single API token, structurally simpler than CrowdStrike's OAuth2 flow; Step 1 should read as intentionally simpler, not a trimmed copy
Write-back requires write scope on the same token, detected separately from read-scope capability and must use distinct unavailable-reason copy (license vs. token scope)
Behavior Confidence and Share Risk Signals are mutually exclusive by hard block, not soft warning, and the UI must surface this as an active decision, not passive disabled-state copy alone
Sync and push both run on the same scheduled cadence as Connect Step 3; no real-time implication in either direction

Combined CrowdStrike (6) + Netskope (7) category rows approach the scalability limit of a flat list per competitor-analysis.md; this strategy groups Netskope's own page locally but defers cross-integration restructuring
No competitor, including Living Security, publicly documents admin-tunable weighting or write-back configurability to defer to as a convention
selected_strategy: Two distinct settings pages (Configure Risk Score Weights, Share Risk Signals with Netskope) with an explicit cross-reference at the point of conflict (Option C)
selected_strategy_rationale: Sliders and toggles represent structurally different decisions (how much vs. whether); collapsing them into one page or one control style would misrepresent Share Risk Signals as a weighting decision. Separate pages with an active, modal-driven cross-reference at the exact moment the Behavior Confidence conflict triggers makes the outbound nature and stakes of write-back legible on its own terms, directly countering the competitor-analysis finding that Living Security's public materials describe write-back in outcome language without disclosing configurability.

alternative_strategies.name: Mirrored twin page
alternative_strategies.summary: Build Share Risk Signals as a visually identical settings page to the weights page, differing only in data direction
alternative_strategies.rejected_because: Risks the two pages being mistaken for one continuous configuration surface, obscuring the important incoming-vs-outgoing distinction

alternative_strategies.name: Single combined page with tab/section split
alternative_strategies.summary: One Netskope settings page with 'Pull from Netskope' and 'Push to Netskope' sections
alternative_strategies.rejected_because: Makes the hard-block Behavior Confidence conflict easier to miss in a long scrolling page rather than requiring the admin to confront it directly

tradeoffs: Two separate pages risk under-discovery of the second page; mitigated with a status summary on the Integrations list tile showing both pull-category-count and push-signal-count at a glance
The explicit cross-reference callout and confirmation modal add UI surface area, deliberately, given write-back's third-party enforcement stakes
Deferring cross-integration category grouping (CrowdStrike + Netskope under named dimensions) means this feature ships a locally organized but globally still-flat two-integration surface
assumptions: Admins benefit from a page-local three-cluster grouping (Behavior Confidence / granular categories / No Netskope Visibility) on the weights page, short of full named-dimension restructuring
A confirmation modal, not just disabled-state copy, is warranted for the Behavior Confidence / Share Risk Signals conflict given it silently changes another page's configuration
Dashboard Viewer's read access question should be resolved jointly with CrowdStrike's identical open question, not answered twice
open_issues: Cross-integration category grouping across CrowdStrike and Netskope is out of scope for this strategy and should be its own design pass
No recommended default weight values defined for Netskope's categories
Whether Dashboard Viewer sees a read-only Netskope section on the risk score breakdown is unresolved, mirrors the same open CrowdStrike question
Exact UCI-to-Dune-badge-scale translation formula is an Eng question this strategy explicitly defers
Security review scope for write-back may surface new requirements (e.g. an audit trail of pushed data) not yet designed for
risks: Under-discovery of the Share Risk Signals page if an admin only ever visits the weights page
Getting the UCI-to-Dune-scale translation direction wrong at the display layer would silently invert risk severity for any admin reading the score
Softening the irreversibility warning copy (data already pushed to Netskope cannot be retracted) to match a generic settings-change pattern would understate real stakes
new_patterns_required: Outbound signal configuration page (Share Risk Signals) — first instance of this pattern in Dune's product
next_actions: Build Connect wizard and Configure Risk Score Weights in Figma first, reusing CrowdStrike's components directly
Design Share Risk Signals as the first outbound-signal-configuration pattern instance; treat it as deserving dedicated design review, not a quick derivative of the weights page
Validate the conflict-modal copy with Eng once write-back's security review clarifies consent/audit requirements
Resolve recommended default weights and Dashboard Viewer visibility jointly with the equivalent open CrowdStrike items
